items.name: tobit ll(0)
notes: Stata stores var(e.y)=sigma^2; sqrt + delta method map it to /sigma
Stata's own /sigma standard error is obtained here as se(var(e.y)) / (2*sqrt(var(e.y))), the delta method used by Stata for the sigma row it prints

items.name: tobit /sigma SE root cause (diagnostic)
notes: westata's reported se(/sigma) is the standard error of ln(sigma), not of sigma: against an independent central-difference Hessian it matches the (b, lnsigma) parameterisation to 0.00e+00 and misses the (b, sigma) one by 5.43e-02.
It also reproduces Stata's own se(lnsigma) = se(var(e.y))/(2*var(e.y)) = 0.0383998173 to 2.12e-06, while Stata's se(sigma) = se(var)/(2*sqrt(var)) = 0.0406037441; westata = 0.0383997360.
The ratio is exactly 1/sigma_hat: 0.945719091 vs 1/1.057394212 (rel 2.11e-06).

The point estimate of sigma agrees to 1e-8, so this is purely a reported-SE bug: the coefficient's last element is on the sigma scale while the covariance matrix is still the lnsigma one. Effect on inference: sigma's z/t statistic is overstated by 1/sigma (here 7.9%).

items.name: intreg interval model
notes: intervals: [floor(y*), floor(y*)+1); y*<0 left-censored (lo missing, hi=0)
Stata e(b) colnames are ['x1','x2','_cons','_cons'] -- the /lnsigma row reuses the _cons label; positions taken from the printed table
Stata prints /lnsigma and a derived sigma row; westata reports /lnsigma as a coefficient and e(sigma)

items.name: heckman twostep
items.command: heckman y_sel x1, select(s = z1 z2) twostep
notes: Stata e(b) order from the printed table: y|x1, y|_cons, s|z1, s|z2, s|_cons, then /mills lambda

Stata's two-step store: e(rho), e(sigma), e(lambda), e(selambda). e(sigma) reproduces sqrt(RSS/m + b_lambda^2*mean(lambda(lambda+w))) to rel 1.83e-10 -- it is NOT sqrt(RSS/(m-3)), which is what westata uses for both sigma and rho
the coefficient on lambda agrees to 1e-9 (0.5301503851 vs 0.5301503857); only the derived e(sigma)/e(rho) differ
selection-equation SEs: Stata keeps the plain probit VCE (ratio to 'probit' 0.99998), westata's joint sandwich bread mixes the outcome block in and inflates select:z1 by 6.8%
outcome-block SEs differ by 2-3%: westata's sandwich is a different (M-estimator) approximation from Stata's Heckman corrected VCE
scalar e(rho) rel diff 7.217e-02
scalar e(sigma) rel diff 6.732e-02

items.name: heckman ml
items.command: heckman y_sel x1, select(s = z1 z2)
notes: westata raises UnsupportedError (text above): the estimator is absent, so the gap is coverage, not numerics.
items.error: UnsupportedError: heckman: only method='twostep' is implemented; 'ml' is not. The maximum likelihood variant requires a joint optimisation over beta, gamma and rho together with the bivariate normal probabilities, which has not been implemented or verified against Stata.

items.name: etregress twostep
items.command: etregress y x1, treat(s = z1 z2) twostep
notes: Stata e(b) order: y|x1, y|s, y|_cons, s|z1, s|z2, s|_cons, lambda
Stata's twostep store holds e(rho), e(sigma), e(lambda), e(selambda), e(ll_p) -- e(sigma1)/e(sigma2) do not exist for etregress in 19.5 (full get_ereturn dump in NOTES), so that pair is untestable
westata's e(rho) has the wrong SIGN on two independent DGPs (+0.4283 Stata vs -0.4486 westata here); westata computes rho = -b_ctrl/sigma while Stata's lambda = rho*sigma
scalar e(rho) rel diff 2.047e+00
scalar e(sigma) rel diff 4.516e-02

items.name: etregress ml
items.command: etregress y x1, treat(s = z1 z2)
notes: Stata's DEFAULT for etregress is ML -- 'twostep' is the option that selects the control-function estimator, so westata's only available path is not Stata's default. ML reference:
items.error: UnsupportedError: etregress: only method='control' is implemented; 'ml' is not. The maximum likelihood variant requires the joint likelihood of the outcome and treatment equations with a bivariate normal error term, which has not been implemented or verified against Stata.

items.name: qreg median
notes: two independent LP solutions of the same check-function objective can differ when the optimum is not unique; Stata's 'alternate solutions' warning was not raised for this DGP

items.name: qreg vce(robust) median
notes: at tau=.5, (tau - 1{u<0})^2 == tau(1-tau) for every i, so this point cannot tell the two candidate sandwich meats apart; the .25 case below is the discriminating one

items.name: qreg vce(robust) quantile(.25)
items.command: qreg y x1 x2, quantile(.25) vce(robust)
notes: A = J^-1 M J^-1 with J = sum f_i x x' and M = sum psi_i^2 x x'. Stata's M is tau(1-tau) X'X to 9e-9; westata's psi_i^2 meat is 4.6% off at tau=.25 and 3.5% at tau=.75 (verified separately, see NOTES)

items.name: sqreg q(.25 .5) pooled 4x500
items.command: sqreg y x1 x2, quantile(.25 .5) reps(500)
notes: coefficients are deterministic qreg fits; only the bootstrap VCE can differ
both sides are averaged over 4 seeds x 500 reps (variance average) to remove bootstrap Monte-Carlo error, since Stata's RNG stream cannot be reproduced in numpy
Stata e(b) order is q.25|x1,x2,_cons then q.5|x1,x2,_cons

items.name: bsqreg median pooled 4x500
items.command: bsqreg y x1 x2, quantile(.5) reps(500)
notes: same pooling as sqreg; Stata e(b) order x1, x2, _cons
Stata's bsqreg SE exceeds its own analytic qreg vce(robust) by ~26% on this heteroskedastic DGP, and westata's bootstrap reproduces that, so the two bootstraps agree within MC error (see NOTES)

items.name: rreg hetero DGP
notes: Stata's rreg SE is NOT the pseudovalue (Street-Carroll-Ruppert) estimate: it equals e(rmse) * sqrt(diag((X'X)^-1)) on the unweighted design, reproduced to 1e-16 on all four datasets (extra['stata_se_law'])
westata computes the S-C-R pseudovalue variance instead, which is why its SEs differ; the coefficients agree to ~2e-4
westata reports weighted sums of squares (final biweights); Stata's e(rss)/e(mss)/e(rmse)/e(r2)/e(F) are different quantities, see NOTES
